blocks.text: We have already discussed annihilation of positron-electron pair in the last chapter. Infact, annihilation is an event taking place whenever a particle and its antiparticle come close to each other. In elementary particles research, very high energies are required for investigations. Instead of collisions at their rest mass energies, they are accelerated to nearly the speed of light and then collided. At CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), proton p⁺-antiproton p⁻ and other heavy nuclei are collided at nearly with the speed of light to create conditions similar to early universe. p⁺,-p⁻ and other heavy particles collision at energies of the order of TeV offer insight to early universe conditions. During such collisions electro-weak force mediation particles W⁺, W⁻¹ and Z bosons predicted by Prof. Abdus Salam have been discovered, along with top and bottom quarks and most significant Higgs bosons in July, 2012.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The LHC collides protons with protons (and heavy nuclei such as lead with each other), not protons with antiprotons; proton-antiproton collisions were made at CERN's earlier SPS collider and at Fermilab's Tevatron. The negative W boson is written W⁻, not W⁻¹.

blocks.alt: A W/Z boson at the collision point, surrounded by a spray of small particles, branches into a W/Z boson and a Higgs boson h. The W/Z gives a quark q and an antiquark q-bar; h gives a b and a b-bar quark. Each quark ends in a spray of particles: Jet 1, Jet 2, Jet 3 and Jet 4.

blocks.title: Example 19.4
blocks.problem: Calculate the energy of the gamma ray photons emitted during the annihilation of an electron-positron pair.
steps:
Mass of positron = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg
Mass of electron = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg

Using Einstein mass-energy relation
E = 2mc²
= 2 × 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg × (3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹)²
blocks.answer: Hence 2γ-ray photons will be emitted each with 0.51 MeV energy travelling in opposite directions to conserve momentum.
